name: Baybars and the Mamluk Sultanate's Rise
summary: Baybars, the Mamluk commander who played a decisive role at Ain Jalut (1260), murdered Sultan Qutuz to seize power. As sultan until 1277 he transformed the Mamluk state into the dominant power of the Middle East: he drove Crusaders from several key fortresses, raided Cilician Armenia, and established a shadow Abbasid caliphate in Cairo to give his sultanate Islamic legitimacy. His administrative reforms lasted for generations.
outcomes: Baybars seizes sultanate after Ayn Jalut
Shadow Abbasid caliph installed in Cairo

_quarry.structural_significance: Established the Mamluk Sultanate as the preeminent power in the Islamic Middle East; his systematic reduction of Crusader strongholds foreshadowed their final expulsion.
